review:
An incredibly frustrating puzzle experience. Unlike Sudoku, which this game is clearly inspired by, the game dangles a logical thread in front of you only to tear it away when you start following it. The way the game works is that you have to have one of each number in every row or column, just like Sudoku - though Cross Set gives you predetermined numbers in every slot that you then have to switch. Sometimes some numbers can't be switched and are thus set, and you have to figure out which row or column can only have one solution and work backwards from there.

The issue with that is that this still leaves several rows and columns unaccounted for - so you change some numbers to figure out one row, which then makes another column unviable, so you fix that, but that ruins the first row again, and so forth. Essentially, there is no "puzzling" here - unlike the peaceful, satisfying unraveling that Sudoku gives you, this is just mindless clicking and fixing mistake after mistake until you, eventually, arrive at the solution; that is, if you're lucky enough to not puzzle yourself into a loop. 

There are no hints, the interface is terrible (why aren't solved rows or columns marked to make it easier to see where I may need to change things? Why can't I lock an entire row or column if I need to and have to lock separate cells instead?) and it only took me 25 minutes of puzzling to see that the only challenge in Cross Set is ever bigger fields to puzzle in, which sounds like a nightmare given how annoying even the small levels already were. Puzzle games are most satisfying when you can slowly unravel a solution by following a logical line of "I can only do this, then this, then this" or "What can't I do and what does that mean?" like Sudoku for example where you slowly fill in the board given the variables you have in play. Cross Set simply has way too many such variables present on the field at all time to result into any more than mindless clicking and eye strain because of the amount of numbers present. As a puzzle fan, I would avoid it at all costs.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

A well-made Logic/Puzzle game that reminds the gamer about Sudoku but excluding the boxes inside the puzzle, so you only focus on unique digits up to its dimension (excluding 0 so from 1 to n where n is the number of rows and columns) for each row and column.

 It might sound easy for a small dimension (4x4-grid net), but as you advance to next level, you'll solve puzzles of higher dimension (9x9 is the largest size for this game). Don't worry as you'll know for each grid in the specific puzzle which digits must contain, so you can always rule out the other digits that possibly can fit in other grids. Simple mechanics like locking grids with suggested digits and shifting the choices of digits each grid can have, helps a lot. 

Highly recommended if you are into puzzle games and wants to exercise your brain some puzzles. If you're a achievement hunter though, focus on the first eight levels as the upcoming bonus levels won't have achievements and they are fairly trickier than previous levels but doable.

As many other reviews have said, this game tends to devolve into little more than reading numbers to find the one row or column which has only one of a certain number. It kind of reminded me of how you can brute force a word search by going through each letter. Due to how often this is the case it seems that was the intended way to approach many of these 'puzzles' and it quickly gets dull and repetitive just scanning through the numbers.

In my opinion the most fun levels were the ones which provided a few squares to begin with as they generally consisted of less word-search gameplay and becomes more similar to Sudoku. Unfortunately the last few levels of the largest 9X9 grids have nothing filled in at the start and thus began the tedium of finding the unique number in a row or column. Once you get pretty far into a level it can be sort of fun when you can search around to find which squares have been made solvable, but it doesn't make up for the boring searching you're subjected to most of the time.

This all being said, it is only $0.99 so if it sounds interesting or relaxing to you it's not like it's a huge investment.

Cross Set spielt sich ähnlich wie das klassische Sudoku mit dem Unterschied, dass die 3x3-Quadrat-Regel nicht bindend ist. Lediglich für die horizontalen und vertikalen Reihen gilt die Einmalregel für sämtliche Zahlen. 

Bis auf die späteren Bonus-Level konnte ich auch alles mit genügend Zeit und Konzentration lösen. Unter den Bonus-Leveln gibt es halt ein paar richtig heftige Rätsel. Da könnte ich auch nicht sagen, wie man die lösen soll. Trotz allem hat mir das Spiel Spaß gemacht und ansich hat Cross Set auch genügend gut lösbare Aufgaben für ein Spiel dieser Art. Von daher sehe ich die Bonus-Level auch nur als Bonus für extreme Hardcore-Fans. 

Was man an Cross Set vielleicht kritisieren kann ist, dass man Sudokus und vergleichbare Mathematik-Rätsel auch kostenlos im Netz finden kann. Dafür braucht man nicht wirklich Cross Set. Gemessen an dem Preis von ca. 1 € spielt das allerdings auch keine Rolle. Die Leute, die auf Sudoku und ähnliche Rätsel stehen, sollten eigentlich wissen, worauf Sie sich hierbei einlassen. Für 1 € kann man da schon einmal so einen kleinen Entwickler unterstützen.

A simple but fun game if you like logic puzzles like Sudoku.

Each box shows one or more numbers that can potentially go in that spot, with the largest leftmost number being the one currently selected. So, for example, if a box shows "7 1 5" then 7 is the current selection but you could also change that square to be a 1 or a 5. You can cycle through the numbers in the box with left click. Right click highlights the square in orange and "locks" the selection in. Selections do no have to be locked in to complete the puzzle and they can be unlocked by right clicking again. Once all columns and rows have no more than 1 of each number in them the puzzle is complete.

There are 7 sections with 8 puzzles each and another section with 1 final puzzle. Completing those will unlock bonus puzzles that do not have achievements.

One major drawback of the game is the inability to cross out numbers. For example, if the box shows "7 1 5" and you've determined that it definitely can't be a 1 you don't have any method of marking it off. You just have to remember that or recheck it every time. This can make the puzzles be slightly more frustrating and take much longer than they should.

I'd recommend this game, but even at it's low price point it would probably be better to pick it up on sale. There's just not enough content for $3 and the lack of some method of "marking" the board besides the right-click highlighting make it not quite worth full price.

Jeu de réflexion mathématique qui emprunte beaucoup au Sudoku (beurk), mais en plus guidé (et moins chiant). Le but est de faire apparaitre dans chaque colonnes et chaque lignes, seulement une occurrence de chaque chiffre.

Ça ne vole pas très haut: il n'y a que 3 mécaniques à comprendre avant de rouler sur le jeu, et si les niveaux deviennent de plus en plus grand, ils ne se complexifient pas des masses. En gros, en faisant attention et en restant concentré, il n'y a pas raison de faire d'erreur. Et heureusement, car une erreur se paye chère, puisqu'il faudra recommencer le niveau à zéro, et le début des tableaux est assez fastidieux.

Et pourtant, la sauce prend, je me suis à nouveau retrouvé victime du "encore un petit dernier et j'arrête", puis encore un, etc... En tout, 9h pour boucler le 100% sachant qu'on débloque à la toute fin des niveaux générés aléatoirement. Pas assez accro pour tenter le truc, j'ai vite désinstallé cette drogue, pressé de passer à autre chose.

Sachant qu'il coûte une poignée d'euros, ça peut valoir le coup pour les personnes qui aiment le genre (ou le Sudoku), mais ne vous attendez pas à une révolution.

A relaxing puzzle game with a good progression of difficulty through the levels. I would recommend this to those who enjoy number or logic puzzles, but with three caveats.

(1) A minor one: the music can be repetitive. There aren't many tunes, and the same tune plays throughout a level. So if a particular level is taking a while to solve, it can get annoying. The sound can be turned off (all sounds, not just music) by going back to the main menu; which brings me to the second issue...

(2) A more major one: If you abandon a level part-way through, no progress is saved. This means that on the harder levels you have to solve them in one sitting, or leave the the game running until you come back to it.

(3) A missing feature (IMO): You can lock a cell to the correct number, but you can't remove impossible numbers from a cell; e.g. if the choices are 3, 6 and 8 and you have worked out that it can't be 8, it would be very useful to be able to delete or otherwise mark the 8. With harder levels when cells have three or more digits this missing feature makes it more difficult to solve. In fact, on the later levels I resorted to copying the puzzle into a spreadsheet so that I could do this.

In summary, a game that I enjoyed playing, which could be improved to make it even better.

Я не силён в Судоку, но игра умудрилась своим подобием на неё заинтересовать. Итак, всё в подробностях:

[h1]Геймплей[/h1]
Даётся всего лишь одно поле, на котором представлены цифры:
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1646901820  
Суть проста - сделать так, чтобы по-вертикали и по-горизонтали каждое число встречалось ровно 1 раз, без повторов. В то время, как звучит это просто, со временем появляются более сложные головоломки и встречается меньше зацепок для полноценной разгадки головоломок. Очень большую роль здесь играет внимательность: сделав всего одну ошибку, всё решение головоломки может отправиться на свалку (если только вы своевременно не обнаружите ошибку), а с ним и размышления над головоломкой. Именно после таких моментов и хочется сделать небольшую паузу и вернуться в следующий раз, в надежде на правильное решение головоломки.
Часть головоломок может уже на старте давать некоторые подсказки:
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1646901981  
Ничего плохого в этом нет и геймплею ровным счётом не мешает.

[h1]Управление[/h1]
Левой кнопкой мыши - меняется число в ячейке (среди доступных в ней же), правой - красим ячейку и фиксируем её. Это не гарантирует правильность решения, но очень полезно при полной концентрации на игре.

[h1]Уровни[/h1]
Всего представлено 57 уровней (7 по 8 и финальный). Сложнее всего попадаются уровни в районе Х-7, 8, однако бывают и исключения.

[h1]Музыка[/h1]
В принципе не является чем-то напряжённым при игре, однако бывают моменты, когда это начинает мешать и из-за этого можешь нечаянно совершить ошибку. Это редкость, но имеет место быть.

[h1]Итог[/h1]
Очень грамотная реализация подобия Судоку, оставив всего лишь одно-единственное поле и задав туда различные варианты цифр. Голова не болит, но мозги кипят и происходит это с удовольствием.

[h1]Вердикт[/h1]
Знаете ли вы Судоку или нет - это не имеет разницы. К покупке рекомендую при любом раскладе.

Another minimalistic puzzle game that I was able to pick up on sale awhile ago... I was able to pick this up for 40% which is a bit worse than what the holiday sale gives but for such a low price the game is well worth it no matter what price you get it at. The game is similar to a sudoku game with a little bit more simplicity, and while I was playing I was stuck between having the simplicity as a pro or a con, and I eventually decided that it was more of a pro than it was a con. Anyways, here's a list of pros and cons about the game.

Pros:

- Simplicity
Many games like this might have tools that help you make the game easier (for example, when you lock in a number remove others of the same number from other squares) and while playing this game I wasn't sure if this was good or bad for the game. In the end I decided that I enjoyed it because it kept the game more difficult and made you think that extra bit.

- Good soundtrack
The soundtrack was nice background music and helped to preserve that "zen feeling" that you got when you were playing this game.

- Achievements
The achievements along the way were nice and popped at the precise moment that they were needed. It was nice finishing a level and reading "Level 5 unlocked" and then a few seconds later seeing the achievement pop up on the bottom right.

Cons:

- Tedious
While this isn't a huge con I felt like the game was a tad bit repetitious at times. You'd go from a difficult level (4th one in the pack) to an easy level and wouldn't get back up to the difficulty until the 7th or 8th pack... for all of the level packs. It would have been nice to introduce something (I don't know what) that made the game mechanic feel a little bit different.

Overall however, I really enjoyed the game for the price I got it at, and I think this one would be worth the full price even on sale! The 3 dollar price tag for ~4-5 hours of entertainment is definitely a big thumbs up for this game. I'd give this one a 9/10 and it definitely earns my thumbs up!

A decent puzzle game that is similar in style to Sudoku, in that you are given a set of numbers and must ensure each row and column contain one of each number. The puzzles vary in size, up to 9x9, but are not as complicated as Sudoku puzzles (those which also require you to complete nine individual boxes of 1-9, in addition to rows and columns).

As a simplified Sudoku game, each level is generally quick to solve. With a total of 64 puzzles, it likely won't take more than a few hours to complete the game. But the replay value is the same as any Sudoku or similarly-styled number game.

The game allows you to lock in numbers that you're certain are correct, but locking-in numbers isn't required to complete the puzzles. This game could be improved with a couple small QOL features such as the ability to save your progress on a partially-completed level, and the ability to strike-out numbers on individual tiles that you've deemed to be incorrect... but overall I'd say this game is worth the $3 price tag, and very much worth a buy if on sale.

[h1]Description[/h1]

Cross Set is a sudoku-like puzzle where the objective is to make sure digits appear only once horizontally and vertically in the grid. The tweak is that the available digits for each cell are limited and displayed. Your job is thus to cycle through the digits in the cells, use logic and right-click the cells you're sure you've solved until you've completed the level.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*] Tweak on sudoku making it fresh again
[*] Good difficulty curve through levels
[*] Decent amount of content for the price, especially when factoring in the bonus levels
[/list]

[h1]Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*] Color scheme and contrasted background might hurt your eyes (they sure made my vision blurry)
[*] Some levels are exceptionally difficult and a bit frustrating
[*] Missed opportunity for an easier mode where the game would warn you when you make mistakes
[/list]

[h1]Verdict[/h1]

If you're a sudoku or a puzzle game addict, Cross Set will probably be worth your while, especially on sale. But do stare at a screenshot long enough to make sure it will not be as visually uncomfortable for you as it was for me.

Ein schönes und gutes Zahlenrätselspiel mit starken Ähnlichkeiten zu Sodoku.
In einem rechteckigen Brett sind mehrere Felder und in jedem Feld sind eine oder mehrere Ziffern.
Wenn es mehrere sind, dann muß man eine Ziffer so auswählen, daß am Ende in den Feldern jeder Zeile und jeder Spalte jede Ziffer genau einmal auftaucht.
Dies wird im Laufe der Zeit immer kniffliger und man muß genau überlegen.
Alle Rätsel lassen sich durch nachdenken lösen.
Eine von den Ziffern ist immer hervorgehoben und wenn man sicher ist die richtige ausgewählt zu haben, kann man das Feld als gelöst markieren.
In einem einzelnem Level kann nicht zwischengespeichert werden.

[u]Kleine Schwäche bei Teilergebnissen[/u]
Wenn man in einem Feld mit 4 Ziffern die Hälfte ausschliessen kann, würde man auf Papier sie einfach durchstreichen. Hier gibt das Programm keine entsprechende Hilfe und man muß es sich merken oder wiederholt sich vieleicht später.
